title: Certifying information flow in multi-agent behaviours
authors: M. Haider Akbar, Onur Pusuluk, Özgür E. Müstecaplıoğlu
abstract: We study which input-output behaviours of several agents can be produced by a declared communication schedule, that is, a fixed sequence of senders, recipients, message alphabets, and output times, together with shared randomness. Since a schedule admits only finitely many deterministic protocols, membership is a linear program, and an infeasible target is excluded by a separating inequality. Under explicit operational assumptions, we prove that the affine hull of the achievable behaviours is described exactly by the equalities stating that each joint output statistic depends only on the inputs that can reach the agents involved, so that a violated equality identifies both the statistic and the missing input. One binary message per event already attains this affine hull, so message capacity restricts which behaviours are achievable without being visible to any equality. We apply the result to one-bit broadcast and relay hierarchies for two and three agents, and to low-order projections of the local polytope.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a framework to certify information flow in multi-agent systems by analyzing the polytope of achievable input-output behaviors. It proves that the set of possible behaviors is constrained by algebraic equalities derived from input reachability, rather than just inequalities imposed by capacity. This provides a powerful tool for understanding the fundamental limits of distributed computation and communication.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize the set of achievable input-output behaviors in multi-agent communication protocols given a fixed communication schedule.
main_result: The affine hull of achievable behaviors is determined exactly by reachability constraints, meaning joint statistics only depend on inputs that can reach the involved agents.
method: The authors use moment coordinates, convex hull analysis, and linear programming duality to establish necessary and sufficient conditions for behavioral achievability.
model_or_system: The model consists of multi-agent systems with binary inputs and outputs, governed by a fixed communication schedule involving senders, recipients, and message alphabets.
key_observables: Joint output statistics, moment coordinates (e.g., $E_S(\mathbf{x})$), and the dimension of the local polytope projection.
important_parameters: Message capacity, the order of the moment statistics ($K$), and the specific structure of the communication schedule.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on explicit operational assumptions regarding the communication schedule and the use of shared randomness.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time-unrolled two-bit relay structure, showing how reachability sets determine dependencies, and a flow chart summarizes the certification procedure.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by introducing moment coordinates, establishing the main theorem relating the affine hull to reachability, and then applying this framework to worked examples like two- and three-agent relays to distinguish between direct and parity readouts.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical characterization of information flow constraints using moment methods is highly relevant for understanding the limits of quantum communication protocols and device-independent security proofs.
